sourceChapterWithLineNumbers:
1:   Arjuna.
2:   Now would I hear, O gracious Kesava![FN#26]
3:   Of Life which seems, and Soul beyond, which sees,
4:   And what it is we know-or think to know.
5: 
6:   Krishna.
7:   Yea! Son of Kunti! for this flesh ye see
8:   Is Kshetra, is the field where Life disports;
9:   And that which views and knows it is the Soul,
10:   Kshetrajna. In all "fields," thou Indian prince!
11:   I am Kshetrajna. I am what surveys!
12:   Only that knowledge knows which knows the known
13:   By the knower![FN#27] What it is, that "field" of life,
14:   What qualities it hath, and whence it is,
15:   And why it changeth, and the faculty
16:   That wotteth it, the mightiness of this,
17:   And how it wotteth-hear these things from Me!
18: 
19:   .     .     .     .     .     .     .     .     .     .     .     .[FN#28]
20: 
21: 
22:   The elements, the conscious life, the mind,
23:   The unseen vital force, the nine strange gates
24:   Of the body, and the five domains of sense;
25:   Desire, dislike, pleasure and pain, and thought
26:   Deep-woven, and persistency of being;
27:   These all are wrought on Matter by the Soul!
28: 
29:   Humbleness, truthfulness, and harmlessness,
30:   Patience and honour, reverence for the wise.
31:   Purity, constancy, control of self,
32:   Contempt of sense-delights, self-sacrifice,
33:   Perception of the certitude of ill
34:   In birth, death, age, disease, suffering, and sin;
35:   Detachment, lightly holding unto home,
36:   Children, and wife, and all that bindeth men;
37:   An ever-tranquil heart in fortunes good
38:   And fortunes evil, with a will set firm
39:   To worship Me--Me only! ceasing not;
40:   Loving all solitudes, and shunning noise
41:   Of foolish crowds; endeavours resolute
42:   To reach perception of the Utmost Soul,
43:   And grace to understand what gain it were
44:   So to attain,--this is true Wisdom, Prince!
45:   And what is otherwise is ignorance!
46: 
47:   Now will I speak of knowledge best to know-
48:   That Truth which giveth man Amrit to drink,
49:   The Truth of HIM, the Para-Brahm, the All,
50:   The Uncreated;; not Asat, not Sat,
51:   Not Form, nor the Unformed; yet both, and more;--
52:   Whose hands are everywhere, and everywhere
53:   Planted His feet, and everywhere His eyes
54:   Beholding, and His ears in every place
55:   Hearing, and all His faces everywhere
56:   Enlightening and encompassing His worlds.
57:   Glorified in the senses He hath given,
58:   Yet beyond sense He is; sustaining all,
59:   Yet dwells He unattached: of forms and modes
60:   Master, yet neither form nor mode hath He;
61:   He is within all beings--and without--
62:   Motionless, yet still moving; not discerned
63:   For subtlety of instant presence; close
64:   To all, to each; yet measurelessly far!
65:   Not manifold, and yet subsisting still
66:   In all which lives; for ever to be known
67:   As the Sustainer, yet, at the End of Times,
68:   He maketh all to end--and re-creates.
69:   The Light of Lights He is, in the heart of the Dark
70:   Shining eternally. Wisdom He is
71:   And Wisdom's way, and Guide of all the wise,
72:   Planted in every heart.
73: 
74:   So have I told
75:   Of Life's stuff, and the moulding, and the lore
76:   To comprehend. Whoso, adoring Me,
77:   Perceiveth this, shall surely come to Me!
78: 
79:   Know thou that Nature and the Spirit both
80:   Have no beginning! Know that qualities
81:   And changes of them are by Nature wrought;
82:   That Nature puts to work the acting frame,
83:   But Spirit doth inform it, and so cause
84:   Feeling of pain and pleasure. Spirit, linked
85:   To moulded matter, entereth into bond
86:   With qualities by Nature framed, and, thus
87:   Married to matter, breeds the birth again
88:   In good or evil yonis.[FN#29]
89: 
90:   Yet is this
91:   Yea! in its bodily prison!--Spirit pure,
92:   Spirit supreme; surveying, governing,
93:   Guarding, possessing; Lord and Master still
94:   PURUSHA, Ultimate, One Soul with Me.
95: 
96:   Whoso thus knows himself, and knows his soul
97:   PURUSHA, working through the qualities
98:   With Nature's modes, the light hath come for him!
99:   Whatever flesh he bears, never again
100:   Shall he take on its load. Some few there be
101:   By meditation find the Soul in Self
102:   Self-schooled; and some by long philosophy
103:   And holy life reach thither; some by works:
104:   Some, never so attaining, hear of light
105:   From other lips, and seize, and cleave to it
106:   Worshipping; yea! and those--to teaching true--
107:   Overpass Death!
108: 
109:   Wherever, Indian Prince!
110:   Life is--of moving things, or things unmoved,
111:   Plant or still seed--know, what is there hath grown
112:   By bond of Matter and of Spirit: Know
113:   He sees indeed who sees in all alike
114:   The living, lordly Soul; the Soul Supreme,
115:   Imperishable amid the Perishing:
116:   For, whoso thus beholds, in every place,
117:   In every form, the same, one, Living Life,
118:   Doth no more wrongfulness unto himself,
119:   But goes the highest road which brings to bliss.
120:   Seeing, he sees, indeed, who sees that works
121:   Are Nature's wont, for Soul to practise by
122:   Acting, yet not the agent; sees the mass
123:   Of separate living things--each of its kind--
124:   Issue from One, and blend again to One:
125:   Then hath he BRAHMA, he attains!
126: 
127:   O Prince!
128:   That Ultimate, High Spirit, Uncreate,
129:   Unqualified, even when it entereth flesh
130:   Taketh no stain of acts, worketh in nought!
131:   Like to the ethereal air, pervading all,
132:   Which, for sheer subtlety, avoideth taint,
133:   The subtle Soul sits everywhere, unstained:
134:   Like to the light of the all-piercing sun
135:   [Which is not changed by aught it shines upon,]
136:   The Soul's light shineth pure in every place;
137:   And they who, by such eye of wisdom, see
138:   How Matter, and what deals with it, divide;
139:   And how the Spirit and the flesh have strife,
140:   Those wise ones go the way which leads to Life!
141: 
142:   HERE ENDS CHAPTER XIII. OF THE BHAGAVAD-GITA,
143:   Entitled "Kshetrakshetrajnavibhagayog,"
144:   Or "The Book of Religion by Separation of Matter and Spirit."

paratext.text:
Arjuna.
  Now would I hear, O gracious Kesava![FN#26]
  Of Life which seems, and Soul beyond, which sees,
  And what it is we know-or think to know.

HERE ENDS CHAPTER XIII. OF THE BHAGAVAD-GITA,
  Entitled "Kshetrakshetrajnavibhagayog,"
  Or "The Book of Religion by Separation of Matter and Spirit."

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.2 The Blessed Lord said This body, O Arjuna, is called the field; he who knows it is called the knower of the field, by those who know of them.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.2 Lord Shri Krishna replied: O Arjuna! The body of man is the playground of the Self; and That which knows the activities of Matter, sages call the Self.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.2 The Blessed Lord said O son of Kunti, this body is referred to as the 'field'. Those who are versed in this call him who is conscious of it as the 'knower of the field'.

arnold.content:
In all "fields," thou Indian prince!
  I am Kshetrajna. I am what surveys!
  Only that knowledge knows which knows the known
  By the knower![FN#27]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.3 Do thou also know Me as the knower of the field in all fields, O Arjuna. Knowledge of both the field and the knower of the field is considered by Me to be ï1the ï1 knowledge.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.3 I am the Omniscient self that abides in the playground of Matter; knowledge of Matter and of the all-knowing Self is wisdom.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.3 And, O scion of the Bharata dynasty, under-stand Me to be the 'Knower of the field' in all the fields. In My opinion, that is Knowledge which is the knowlege of th field and the knower of the field.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.4 What the field is and of what nature, what are its modifications and whence it is and also who He is and what His powers are hear all that from Me in brief.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.4 What is called Matter, of what it is composed, whence it came, and why it changes, what the Self is, and what Its power - this I will now briefly set forth.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.4 Hear from Me in brief about (all) that as to what that field is and how it is; what its changes are, and from what cause arises what effect; and who He is, and what His powers are.

records.iast:
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam
asaktaṃ sarvabhṛccaiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Glorified in the senses He hath given,
  Yet beyond sense He is; sustaining all,
  Yet dwells He unattached: of forms and modes
  Master, yet neither form nor mode hath He;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.15 Shining by the functions of all the senses, yet without the senses; unattached, yet supporting all; devoid of alities, yet their experiencer.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.15 Beyond the senses, It yet shines through every sense perception. Bound to nothing, It yet sustains everything. Unaffected by the Qualities, It still enjoys them all.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.15 Shining through the functions of all the organs, (yet) devoid of all the organs; unattached, and verily the supporter of all; without ality, and the perceiver of alities;

records.sanskrit:
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च।
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् ॥
records.iast:
bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraṃ carameva ca
sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
He is within all beings--and without--
  Motionless, yet still moving; not discerned
  For subtlety of instant presence; close
  To all, to each; yet measurelessly far!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.16 Without and within (all) beings the unmoving and also the moving; because of Its subtlety, unknowable; and near and far away is That.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.16 It is within all beings, yet outside; motionless yet moving; too subtle to be perceived; far away yet always near.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.16 Existing outside and inside all beings; moving as well as non-moving, It is incomprehensible due to subtleness. So also, It is far away, and yet near.

records.sanskrit:
अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम्।
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥
records.iast:
avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam
bhūtabhartṛ ca tajjñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Not manifold, and yet subsisting still
  In all which lives; for ever to be known
  As the Sustainer, yet, at the End of Times,
  He maketh all to end--and re-creates.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.17 And undivided, yet It exists as if divided in beings; It is to be known as the supporter of being; It devours and It generates.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.17 In all beings undivided, yet living in division, It is the upholder of all, Creator and Destroyer alike;

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.17 And the Knowable, though undivided, appears to be existing as divided in all beings, and It is the sustainer of all beings as also the devourer and originator.

records.sanskrit:
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते।
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम् ॥
records.iast:
jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The Light of Lights He is, in the heart of the Dark
  Shining eternally. Wisdom He is
  And Wisdom's way, and Guide of all the wise,
  Planted in every heart.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.18 That, the Light of all lights, is said to be beyond darkness: knowledge, the knowable and the goal of knowledge, seated in the hearts of all.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.18 It is the Light of lights, beyond the reach of darkness; the Wisdom, the only thing that is worth knowing or that wisdom can teach; the Presence in the hearts of all.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.18 That is the Light even of the lights; It is spoken of as beyond darkness. It is Knowledge, the Knowable, and the Known. It exists specially [A variant reading is dhisthitam.-Tr.] in the hearts of all.

records.sanskrit:
इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः।
मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते ॥
records.iast:
iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ
madbhakta etadvijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
So have I told
  Of Life's stuff, and the moulding, and the lore
  To comprehend. Whoso, adoring Me,
  Perceiveth this, shall surely come to Me!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.19 Thus the field, as well as knowledge and the knowable have been briefly stated. My devotee, knowing this, enters into My Being.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.19 Thus I have told thee in brief what Matter is, and the Self worth realising and what is Wisdom. He who is devoted to Me knows; and assuredly he will enter into Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.19 Thus has been spoken of in brief the field as also Knowledge and the Knowable. By understanding this My devotee becomes alified for My state.

records.sanskrit:
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि।
विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसम्भवान् ॥
records.iast:
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhyanādi ubhāvapi
vikārāṃśca guṇāṃścaiva viddhi prakṛtisambhavān
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.20 Know thou that Nature (matter) and the Spirit are both beginningless; and know also that all modifications and alities are born of Nature.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.20 Know thou further that Nature and God have no beginning; and that differences of character and quality have their origin in Nature only.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.20 Know both Nature and also the individual soul [Prakrti is sometimes translated as matter, and purusa as spirit.-Tr.] to be verily without beginning; know the modifications as also the alities as born of Nature.

records.sanskrit:
कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते।
पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते ॥
records.iast:
kāryakāraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtirucyate
puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve heturucyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
That Nature puts to work the acting frame,
  But Spirit doth inform it, and so cause
  Feeling of pain and pleasure.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.21 In the production of the effect and the cause, Nature (matter) is said to be the cause; in the experience of pleasure and pain, the soul is said to be the cause.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.21 Nature is the Law which generates cause and effect; God is the source of the enjoyment of all pleasure and pain.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.21 With regard to the source of body and organs, Nature is said to be the cause. The soul is the cause so far as enjoyership of happiness and sorrow is concerned.

records.sanskrit:
पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान्।
कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥
records.iast:
puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijānguṇān
kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo.asya sadasadyonijanmasu
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Spirit, linked
  To moulded matter, entereth into bond
  With qualities by Nature framed, and, thus
  Married to matter, breeds the birth again
  In good or evil yonis.[FN#29]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.22 The soul seated in Nature experiences the alities born of Nature; attachment to the alities is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.22 God dwelling in the heart of Nature experiences the Qualities which nature brings forth; and His affinity towards the Qualities is the reason for His living in a good or evil body.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.22 Since the soul is seated in Nature, therefore it experiences the alities born of Nature. Contact with the alities is the cause of its births in good and evil wombs.

records.sanskrit:
उपद्रष्टानुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः।
परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः ॥
records.iast:
upadraṣṭānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ
paramātmeti cāpyukto dehe.asminpuruṣaḥ paraḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Yet is this
  Yea! in its bodily prison!--Spirit pure,
  Spirit supreme; surveying, governing,
  Guarding, possessing; Lord and Master still
  PURUSHA, Ultimate, One Soul with Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.23 The Supreme Soul in this body is also called the spectator, the permitter, the supporter, the enjoyer, the great Lord and the Supreme Self.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.23 Thus in the body of man dwells the Supreme God; He who sees and permits, upholds and enjoys, the Highest God and the Highest Self.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.23 He who is the Witness, the Permitter, the Sustainer, the Experiencer, the great Lord, and who is also spoken of as the transcendental Self is the supreme Person in this body.

records.sanskrit:
य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह।
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥
records.iast:
ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥ saha
sarvathā vartamāno.api na sa bhūyo.abhijāyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Whoso thus knows himself, and knows his soul
  PURUSHA, working through the qualities
  With Nature's modes, the light hath come for him!
  Whatever flesh he bears, never again
  Shall he take on its load.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.24 He who thus knows the Spirit and Matter together with the alities, in whatever condition he may be, he is not born again.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.24 He who understands God and Nature along with her qualities, whatever be his condition in life, he comes not again to earth.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.24 He who knows thus the Person and Nature along with the alities will not be born again, in whatever way he may live.

records.sanskrit:
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना।
अन्ये साङ्ख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥
records.iast:
dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecidātmānamātmanā
anye sāṅkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Some few there be
  By meditation find the Soul in Self
  Self-schooled; and some by long philosophy
  And holy life reach thither; some by works:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.25 Some by meditation behold the Self in the self by the self, others by the Yoga of knowledge, and still others by the Yoga of action.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.25 Some realise the Supreme by meditating, by its aid, on the Self within, others by pure reason, others by right action.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.25 Through meditation some realize the Self in (their) intellect with the help of the internal organ; others through Sankhya-yoga, and others through Karma-yoga.

records.sanskrit:
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वान्येभ्य उपासते।
तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥
records.iast:
anye tvevamajānantaḥ śrutvānyebhya upāsate
te.api cātitarantyeva mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Some, never so attaining, hear of light
  From other lips, and seize, and cleave to it
  Worshipping; yea! and those--to teaching true--
  Overpass Death!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.26 Others also, not knowing thus, worship, having heard of It from others; they, too, cross beyond death, regarding what they have heard as the Supreme refuge.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.26 Others again, having no direct knowledge but only hearing from others, nevertheless worship, and they, too, if true to the teachings, cross the sea of death.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.26 Others, agian, who do not know thus, take to thinking after hearing from others; they, too, who are devoted to hearing, certainly overcome death.

records.sanskrit:
यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम्।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ ॥
records.iast:
yāvatsañjāyate kiñcitsattvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam
kṣetrakṣetrajñasaṃyogāttadviddhi bharatarṣabha
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Wherever, Indian Prince!
  Life is--of moving things, or things unmoved,
  Plant or still seed--know, what is there hath grown
  By bond of Matter and of Spirit:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.27 Wherever a being is born, whether unmoving or moving, know thou, O best of the Bharatas (Arjuna), that it is from the union between the field and its knower.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.27 Wherever life is seen in things movable or immovable, it is the joint product of Matter and Spirit.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.27 O scion of the Bharata dynasty, whatever object, moving or non-moving, comes into being, know that to be from the association of the field and the Knower of the field!

records.sanskrit:
समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम्।
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
records.iast:
samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram
vinaśyatsvavinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Know
  He sees indeed who sees in all alike
  The living, lordly Soul; the Soul Supreme,
  Imperishable amid the Perishing:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.28 He sees, who sees the Supreme Lord, existing eally in all beings, the unperishing within the perishing.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.28 He who can see the Supreme Lord in all beings, the Imperishable amidst the perishable, he it is who really sees.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.28 He sees who sees the supreme Lord as existing eally in all beings, and as the Imperishable among the perishable.

records.sanskrit:
समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम्।
न हिनस्त्यात्मनात्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
records.iast:
samaṃ paśyanhi sarvatra samavasthitamīśvaram
na hinastyātmanātmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
For, whoso thus beholds, in every place,
  In every form, the same, one, Living Life,
  Doth no more wrongfulness unto himself,
  But goes the highest road which brings to bliss.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.29 Because he who sees the same Lord eally dwelling everywhere does not destroy the Self by the self; he goes to the highest goal.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.29 Beholding the Lord in all things equally, his actions do not mar his spiritual life but lead him to the height of Bliss.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.29 Since by seeing eally God who is present alike everywhere he does not injure the Self by the Self, therefore he attains the supreme Goal.

records.sanskrit:
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः।
यः पश्यति तथात्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति ॥
records.iast:
prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ
yaḥ paśyati tathātmānamakartāraṃ sa paśyati
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.30 He sees, who sees that all actions are performed by Nature alone and that the Self is actionless.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.30 He who understands that it is only the Law of Nature that brings action to fruition, and that the Self never acts, alone knows the Truth.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.30 And he who sees actions as being done in various ways by Nature itself, and also the Self as the non-agent,-he sees.

records.sanskrit:
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा ॥
records.iast:
yadā bhūtapṛthagbhāvamekasthamanupaśyati
tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma sampadyate tadā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
sees the mass
  Of separate living things--each of its kind--
  Issue from One, and blend again to One:
  Then hath he BRAHMA, he attains!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.31 When a man sees the whole variety of beings as resting in the One, and spreading forth from That alone, he then becomes Brahman.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.31 He who sees the diverse forms of life all rooted in One, and growing forth from Him, he shall indeed find the Absolute.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.31 When one realizes that the state of diversity of living things is rooted in the One, and that their manifestation is also from That, then one becomes identified with Brahman.

records.sanskrit:
अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः।
शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥
records.iast:
anāditvānnirguṇatvātparamātmāyamavyayaḥ
śarīrastho.api kaunteya na karoti na lipyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
O Prince!
  That Ultimate, High Spirit, Uncreate,
  Unqualified, even when it entereth flesh
  Taketh no stain of acts, worketh in nought!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.32 Being without beginning and being devoid of (any) alities, the Supreme Self, imperishable, though dwelling in the body, O Arjuna, neither acts nor is tainted.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.32 The Supreme Spirit, O Prince, is without beginning, without Qualities and Imperishable, and though it be within the body, yet It does not act, nor is It affected by action.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.32 Being without beginning and without alities, O son of Kunti, this immutable, supreme Self does not act. nor is It affected [Also translated as tainted.-Tr.], although existing in the body.

records.sanskrit:
यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते।
सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथात्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
records.iast:
yathā sarvagataṃ saukṣmyādākāśaṃ nopalipyate
sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Like to the ethereal air, pervading all,
  Which, for sheer subtlety, avoideth taint,
  The subtle Soul sits everywhere, unstained:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.33 As the all-pervading ether is not tainted, because of its subtlety, so the Self seated everywhere in the body is not tainted.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.33 As space, though present everywhere, remains by reason of its subtlety unaffected, so the Self, though present in all forms, retains its purity unalloyed.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.33 As the all-pervading space is not defiled, because of its subtlety, similarly the Self, present everywhere in the body [The singular number is used to denote a class, i.e. all bodies. See S.-Tr.], is not defiled.

records.sanskrit:
यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः।
क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥
records.iast:
yathā prakāśayatyekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokamimaṃ raviḥ
kṣetraṃ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
13.34 Just as the one sun illumines the whole world, so also the Lord of the field (Supreme Self)
illumines the whole field, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.34 As the one Sun illuminates the whole earth, so the Lord illumines the whole universe.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.34 As the single sun illumines this whole world, similarly, O descendant of the Bharata dynasty, the Knower of the field illumines the whole field.

records.sanskrit:
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा।
भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥
records.iast:
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorevamantaraṃ jñānacakṣuṣā
bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca ye viduryānti te param
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And they who, by such eye of wisdom, see
  How Matter, and what deals with it, divide;
  And how the Spirit and the flesh have strife,
  Those wise ones go the way which leads to Life!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 13.35 They who, by the eye of knowledge, perceive the distinction between the field and its knower and also the liberation from the Nature of being, go to the Supreme.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 13.35 Those who with the eyes of wisdom thus see the difference between Matter and Spirit, and know how to liberate Life from the Law of Nature, they attain the Supreme."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 13.35 Those who know thus through the eye of wisdom the distinction between the field and the Knower of the field, and the annihilation of the Matrix of beings,-they reach the Supreme.
